page.text:
The fundamental theorem of arithmetic states that every integer greater
than one is a product of primes, uniquely up to the order of the factors.
This multiplicative classification does not make additive questions about
primes easy. Results proving infinitely many prime pairs within a fixed
bounded distance likewise do not imply that the distance two occurs
infinitely often.
